findings_qualitative.value: The four newly observed debris discs all have low grain size distribution parameters (q < 3.2), suggesting colliding bodies have lower tensile strength and clumping is dominated by self-gravity.

evidence.quote: We present the longest wavelength observations to date of HD 48370, CPD-72 2713, HD 131488, and HD 32297 at 8.8 mm, and find that the $q$ value of these sources are all quite low ($q < 3.2$), suggesting that the colliding bodies in these discs have a lower tensile strength and clumping is dominated by self-gravity.

findings_qualitative.value: There may exist two distributions of q in the debris disc sample: a broad distribution (q ~ 3.2-3.7) for typical gas-poor discs and a narrow distribution (q < 3.2) for bright gas-rich discs, or alternatively an observational bias against detecting faint discs with steep size distributions at cm wavelengths.

evidence.quote: We suggest the possibility of two distributions of $q$ in our debris disc sample; a broad distribution (where $q \sim 3.2-3.7$) for "typical" debris discs (gas-poor/non-detection), and a narrow distribution (where $q < 3.2$) for bright gas-rich discs.

Or alternatively, we suggest that there exists an observational bias between the grain size distribution parameter and absolute flux which may be attributed to the detection rates of faint debris discs at $\rm \sim$cm wavelengths.

claims.hypothesis: The grain size distribution index q in HD 48370, CPD-72 2713, HD 131488, and HD 32297 traces the material properties and collisional regime of parent planetesimals.
claims.experiment: Combine new 8.8 mm ATCA continuum flux measurements with 1.3 mm ALMA fluxes and SED-fitted dust temperatures to calculate q for the four discs.
claims.result: All four targets have q < 3.2, falling within the range predicted by Pan & Sari (2005) (2.88 < q < 3.14).
claims.finding: The colliding bodies in these four discs have a lower tensile strength and clumping is dominated by self-gravity.

evidence.quote: The $q$ values derived for our new ATCA observations all fall within the range predicted by (cite: 2005Icar..173..342P). This suggests that the colliding bodies in these discs have a lower tensile strength and clumping is dominated by self-gravity, resulting in a shallower size distribution.

We present the longest wavelength observations to date of HD 48370, CPD-72 2713, HD 131488, and HD 32297 at 8.8 mm, and find that the $q$ value of these sources are all quite low ($q < 3.2$), suggesting that the colliding bodies in these discs have a lower tensile strength and clumping is dominated by self-gravity.

claims.hypothesis: The grain size distribution power-law index q correlates with host star age and spectral type.
claims.experiment: Perform Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) tests on the 22-disc sample separated by age at 50 Myr and by spectral type (A-F vs G-K-M stars).
claims.result: K-S tests yield a 62% probability of being drawn from the same distribution for the age split, and a 23% probability for the spectral type split.
claims.finding: There is no correlation with age, and the tentative trend with spectral type becomes weaker with a larger sample and is likely to disappear.

evidence.quote: Separating our sample at 50Myr (see Table [\[tab:disc_c\]](#tab:disc_c) for target ages), a Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test estimates a probability of 62% that these two populations are drawn from the same distribution.
Separating our sample by A-F stars and G-(K-M) stars, a K-S test estimates a probability of 23% that these two populations are drawn from the same distribution.
we suggest that as the later star debris disc sample becomes more populated it’s likely that the trend between $q$ and the spectral type will disappear.

claims.hypothesis: Bright gas-rich debris discs and typical gas-poor debris discs have distinct distributions of the grain size distribution parameter q.
claims.experiment: Perform Fisher's exact tests on the 22-disc sample separated at q = 3.2 and categorized either by distance-scaled 1 mm flux at 30 mJy or by gas-rich vs gas-poor status.
claims.result: Fisher's exact test yields p = 0.013 when separated by brightness at 30 mJy and q = 3.2, and p = 0.04 when categorized by gas-rich vs gas-poor.
claims.finding: There may exist two distributions of q (q ~ 3.2-3.7 for typical gas-poor discs and q < 3.2 for bright gas-rich discs), or alternatively an observational sensitivity bias against faint discs with steep size distributions at cm wavelengths.

evidence.quote: We first separate the groups at $q$=3.2 and categorise the targets above and below 30 mJy (effectively separating our gas-rich discs and gas-poor/non-detection discs based on brightness), we obtain a significance of $p=0.013$. If we instead categorise for gas-rich and gas-poor (which doesn’t take the brightness into account) we obtain a lower significance of $p=0.04$.

We suggest possibility of two distributions of $q$; a broad distribution (where $q \sim 3.2-3.7$) for "typical" debris discs (gas-poor/non-detection), and a lower distribution (where $q < 3.2$) for bright gas-rich discs.

Or alternatively, we suggest an observational bias may be present between the grain size distribution parameter and absolute flux which is likely attributed to the detection rates of faint debris discs at $\rm \sim$cm wavelengths.

why_this_data.value: Observing at ~1 cm (8.8 mm) provides a long lever arm with 1.3 mm ALMA data to constrain the mm spectral index alpha_mm and is effectively in the Rayleigh-Jeans regime for typical disk temperatures.

evidence.quote: Despite their faint emission, observing at longer wavelengths ($\rm \sim$1 cm) provides a better constraint on the mm spectral index (a long lever arm) and is effectively in the Rayleigh-Jeans regime for typical disk temperatures.

The PLATYPUS sample are selected to have (1) declinations below 20 degrees in order to be observable with the ATCA array, (2) complementary ALMA observations at 1.3 mm, and (3) are relatively compact to maximize surface brightness sensitivity.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Two-component vs single-component modified blackbody SED fits: two disc components are used only where a significantly better fit is found (HD 131488 and HD 32297).

evidence.quote: Where a significantly better fit is found, two disc components are used (cite: 2009ApJ...701.1367C; 2014MNRAS.444.3164K), though here we are focused on the parameters of the cooler component which contributes to the sub-mm and mm flux.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Observational bias vs two intrinsic populations of q: the correlation between q and flux could be an observational sensitivity bias against faint discs with steep spectral slopes rather than two distinct physical distributions.

evidence.quote: Or alternately given that our systems are faint in apparent flux, it is possible that an observational bias exists, especially since the Pearson coefficient becomes weaker once we scale the flux with the distance.

limitations_admitted.value: Unable to confirm or rule out contamination from stellar emission at 8.8 mm without resolved observations or temporal monitoring, though no strong short (<15 min) flares were seen.

evidence.quote: We are unable to confirm the presence of stellar emission in our detections. To check for other forms of long wavelength emission in our sources, either resolved observations or temporal monitoring is required (cite: 2017MNRAS.466.4083U).

limitations_admitted.value: The modified blackbody break wavelength lambda_0 is essentially unconstrained because the targets have shallow mm-wave slopes (beta close to zero).
